title: Research Methodology
description:
Topic list taken from **7th Semester (FINAL SYLLABUS)** — thirteen topics split between two instructors, **SHS** and **MM**.

The syllabus links two material folders:

- [Lecture Materials — updated 15/12/2025](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mANqmFCSHcEbZDr3DGQWxGh5juIXc-YY)
- [Reading Materials](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Bk9PlJGvVBknAZHi5PbgVmYlPX3jJPbW)

Neither folder was readable from here, so nothing has been imported from them yet.

> **Note on this course:** unlike 401 and 403, this one is taught topic-by-topic rather than chapter-by-chapter, and only four topics have a named reading. Expect the exam to reward structure and vocabulary over derivation.

examPattern.notes: **Placeholder — replace once you have a past paper.** Methodology papers at this level usually mix short definitional answers with one or two design questions ("propose a research design for …"). Record the real structure here so mock papers match it.

sections.name: Section B — Long answer / research design

chapters.title: Introduction to Research
chapters.summary: What counts as research, and the paradigms behind it.

chapters.title: Research Problem and Research Question(s)
chapters.summary: Turning a broad interest into a researchable, answerable question.

chapters.title: Reviewing Literature and Identifying Contribution
chapters.summary: Reading the field well enough to locate the gap your work fills.

chapters.title: Qualitative Research Techniques
chapters.summary: Interviewing, focus groups, ethnography and case study design.

chapters.title: Quantitative Techniques for Non-Causal Research
chapters.summary: Descriptive and associational work: when correlation is the honest claim.

chapters.title: Qualitative Methods in Data Collection and Analysis
chapters.summary: Fieldwork practice, coding, thematic analysis and trustworthiness.

chapters.title: Quantitative Research Techniques (Causal)
chapters.summary: The experimental ideal, regression, instrumental variables and fixed effects / difference-in-differences.

chapters.title: Sampling Design and Data Collection
chapters.summary: Probability and non-probability sampling, sample size, and instrument design.

chapters.title: Research Ethics (1 and 2)
chapters.summary: Two sessions: informed consent, confidentiality, harm, and research integrity.

chapters.title: Data Cleaning
chapters.summary: Missing values, outliers, consistency checks and a reproducible cleaning log.

chapters.title: Data Analysis
chapters.summary: Choosing the analysis that answers the question you actually asked.

chapters.title: Presenting Research
chapters.summary: Structuring a paper, tables and figures, and defending the work.

textbooks.title: Research Methodology: A Step-by-Step Guide for Beginners
textbooks.author: Ranjit Kumar
textbooks.notes: The syllabus cites only these two chapters, but the book's operational-definition and variable-measurement material is the fastest way into topics 9 and 11 as well.

textbooks.title: Qualitative Research Methods for the Social Sciences
textbooks.author: Howard Lune & Bruce L. Berg
textbooks.notes: The syllabus prints this as *"Luna Berg"* — almost certainly **Lune & Berg**. Confirm the edition with your instructor before buying, since the chapter numbering moves between editions.

textbooks.title: Mostly Harmless Econometrics: An Empiricist's Companion
textbooks.author: Joshua D. Angrist & Jörn-Steffen Pischke
textbooks.notes: Chapters 2–5 are the experimental ideal, regression, instrumental variables, and fixed effects / differences-in-differences. **Verify which Angrist & Pischke book is meant** — the same authors' *Mastering 'Metrics* covers the same ground more gently, and the syllabus does not name the title.
